newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent under pressure, other NSea grades quiet.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent under pressure, other NSea grades quiet.

text.p: Dated Brent was under pressure on Tuesday with two end-August cargoes still unsold but other North Sea grades were solid in very quiet business, traders said.

The Aug 28-30 and Aug 29-31 cargoes were last heard offered at 35 cents below October, well below the last Brent deal at September -15 cents on Friday. Best offers heard on Monday were in the September -35 cents range.
Cash Brent intermonth spreads were little changed from overnight, with Sept/Oct having drifted off a few cents to -0.13/-0.11 cents in the last 24 hours and Nov/Dec bid a little higher at -8 cents.
Brent's weakness was underlined when two September dates turning wet on Monday were five o'clocked.
At least one of the two Sept 2-4 cargoes was deferred to Tuesday, the other holder was undecided and another date, Sept 3-5, turns wet today.
Outright crude was improving, with IPE October Brent up seven cents at 1100 GMT on momentum gathered from Monday's healthy close.
Monday's physical business was unspectacular, with two Statfjord and two Forties cargoes seen changing hands. Early Tuesday non-Brent trade was even quieter with nothing visible.
Short-term swaps were largely unchanged, with next week (Aug 25-29) bid at 30 cents below October and the following week (Sept 1-5) offered at 23 cents.
In the Mediterranean most Urals trade was stalled while dealers await the details of the September loading programmes, due in the coming days.

Kirkuk barrels were on offer from traders, but most end-users with allocations had decided to take them into their systems because they could not secure the premium over the official selling price they wanted on the open market.
